newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain regions close GDP gap versus Europe in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Spain regions close GDP gap versus Europe in 1996.

text.p: Spanish regions reduced the economic gap versus the rest of Europe in 1996, a study conducted by saving banks association CECA showed on Tuesday.
In the last few years Spanish regions have also narrowed the gap among themselves, the study added.

"Beside Asturias and Cantabria, all Spanish regions grew by more than the European average in 1996. We can say that all Spanish regions reduced the gap with Europe," Victorio Vaya, general director of CECA, told reporters.
He added that the 1996 European average GDP growth stands at 1.3 percent.

"From 1983 to 1996 Spanish regions have reduced the differences among themsleves. We had regions such as Extremadura and Castille-La Mancha recovering versus the Spanish average and others such as Catalonia worsening" said Julio Alcaide, chief economist of CECA, association of Spanish saving banks.
In 1996, Extremadura had the highest rate of growth standing at 6.6 percent. Asturias had the lowest at 0.5 percent.
Regions with higher growth in 1996 were the ones benefitting from a sharp recovery in agriculture, such as Extremadura, Castille-La Mancha and Castille-Leon.
The Balearic Islands and the Canaries grew thanks to tourism, while Asturias was punished by the weakening of the mining sectors.
The Balearic Islands region is the richest Spanish region, the only one standing above the European average.
